solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stand up to work, then sit

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Advice for a protester: get your job done, then stage a sit-in.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up to someone is to resist or confront them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sides engaged in quoits start to polish deck?

indicators.note: engaged in means taken inside, so the side letters go within the rings

parts.note: quoits are rings, each O-shaped
right and left sides, R and L

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Players of a ring-tossing game begin to clean up the ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest deck of a sailing ship has this name, so it is one example of a deck.

clue.text: Reward boy carrying ordinary cargo

parts.note: to pay is to reward

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the boy word holds the next piece

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad is rewarded for carrying everyday goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The load a vehicle carries, its freight, is its cargo.

clue.text: Band's brief gesture on leaving?

parts.note: brief means short
one waves goodbye when leaving

explanation.surface: A pop group gives a quick goodbye as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is a radio frequency band, not a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio wavelength range between about 10 and 100 metres is one frequency band.

clue.text: Small child loves Latin tutor

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so two loves give two zero-shaped Os

explanation.surface: A young pupil is fond of the language of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tutor' is a verb here: to instruct or train.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or educate them, the verb sense of tutor.

clue.text: Traverse tip of Antarctic sea there

indicators.note: tip of here means the final end letter of the word

parts.note: the Ross Sea is part of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: Crossing the edge of the Antarctic sea in polar exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross something is to go over it from side to side.

clue.text: Old ass rises and leaves for kitchen

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an onager is an Asian wild ass

explanation.surface: An aged donkey gets up and goes off to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried foliage of this herb is used in cooking.

clue.text: Long sentence's right in biography

parts.note: a life sentence is a long prison term; with the 's this gives LIFES
a Tory belongs to the political right

explanation.surface: A life term in prison features in a published account of someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is an account of someone's whole life, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Amuse oneself by winning over Romeo

parts.note: to amuse oneself is to play

indicators.note: winning in the sense of gaining or taking in, so the word by takes in the next piece

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a game in which they win and woo a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover, is a womaniser, much as a rich pleasure-seeking man is.

clue.text: Nearly twelve on holiday take five?

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: twelve is a dozen
someone on holiday is off work

explanation.surface: Near midnight on vacation, someone takes a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take five' means take a short break; the question mark flags the jokey extension to having a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking five minutes' rest can mean nodding into a brief nap, the idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Orange mob scattered, throwing missile

indicators.note: scattered means dispersed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Loyalist marchers disperse as a projectile is hurled.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orange mob suggests Northern Ireland's Orange Order marchers.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Australian weapon is thrown, a missile designed to return.

clue.text: Distributes software current playwright's penning

parts.note: an app is a piece of software

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals, so the playwright's name holds the next piece

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright; with the 's this gives ORTONS
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes and distributes computer software.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to share out or allocate in portions, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A bit of storage space back in place of altar

indicators.note: back means the extracted letters are read in the opposite direction
a bit of these words means some of their letters are taken out of them

explanation.surface: Seeking a little room behind the cupboard for storing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' takes ESPA from 'storagE SPAce'; 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church traditionally houses the altar.

clue.text: Minute assistant withdraws papers etc

indicators.note: withdraws means pulls back, so the helper's word is read backwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A tiny helper retreats from the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers along with broadcasting make up the press and other mass communications collectively.

clue.text: Big Eddy, top musician, hogs large mike

indicators.note: hogs means keeps to itself, so the musician word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a maestro is a distinguished musician
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer named Eddy, a star performer, keeps a big microphone to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a name but is a swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool is a large swirling eddy in the sea.

clue.text: Ring prof who's after forest food for ancient herbivore

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces behind the forest food in the answer

parts.note: mast is the nuts of beech, oak and other forest trees, eaten by pigs
a ring is O-shaped
a don is a university teacher or professor

explanation.surface: Phone a professor who is looking for something to eat in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mast' is the fallen nuts of forest trees, pig food.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct elephant-like animal lived on plants, so it is an ancient plant-eater.

clue.text: Spar alone had packed in broadcast TV

indicators.note: packed in means placed inside, so the word had goes within the next

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A boxer trained solo once a televised fight was squeezed into the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests TV but means scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar against an imaginary opponent is solo boxing practice.

clue.text: Female's nursing a big bird? I approve

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one word holds the others

parts.note: female gives HER; the 's means has, linking to what follows
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A woman cradles a large bird, perhaps an ostrich, in her arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary cry of agreement is the spoken way of saying one supports what was said.

clue.text: Began again to think about owing money

indicators.note: to here means attached into, so the reflection word is fitted inside the debt word

parts.note: an account in the red is overdrawn

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to muse is to think

explanation.surface: Someone started worrying once more about their debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a loose container signal here: the reversed thought is fitted into the debt word.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to restart after a pause, so to begin again.

clue.text: Speaker doesn't begin to try

indicators.note: doesn't begin means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Tannoy is a British public-address loudspeaker system

explanation.surface: A speaker fails to make an effort to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the verb as in try one's patience. TANNOY is a British loudspeaker brand.
explanation.definitionFit: To try someone's patience is to irritate or vex them.

clue.text: TV fundraiser given up after husband left memo

indicators.note: in a down clue given up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
left means departed, so the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a telethon is a long charity television broadcast

explanation.surface: A charity broadcast abandoned after a spouse walked out leaving a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops H from TELETHON to give TELETON; 'given up' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A short informal note or folded notepaper is a brief written message.

clue.text: One's reproduced water in Oxford

indicators.note: reproduced means copied, so the piece appears twice

parts.note: one is I; with the 's this gives IS

explanation.surface: Someone's copy is made, perhaps on waters around a university town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames at Oxford is known locally by this name, so it is that city's river.

clue.text: Kitchen expert circles right round celeb

parts.note: a ring is a circle
a round thing is O-shaped
a celeb is a star

explanation.surface: A master chef walks around a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen' looks culinary but is musicians' slang for an orchestra's percussion section; R goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles drummer is a percussion expert, and the kitchen is the drum and percussion section.

clue.text: Regularly trouble earl and monarch

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A king who keeps having disputes with a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign, one who governs a realm.

clue.text: He's habitually early or late for part of flight

definitions.meaning: an early or a late one is a person who habitually gets out of bed at that time
the vertical section of each stair in a staircase

explanation.surface: A man's punctuality issues affect part of his air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright board between treads is part of a staircase, and anyone getting up is one too.

clue.text: Cricket's first law restricts member in crease

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the sport's name is used
restricts means hems in, so the law word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a law is a rule
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cricketing regulation limits how a fielder stands in the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is a line marked on the pitch; here it is a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple is to crush into folds, so to crease or wrinkle.

clue.text: Needle and daggers with sleek edges

parts.note: obeli are dagger-shaped printers' marks, plural of obelus

indicators.note: edges means only the first and last letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Weapons honed to a polished sharpness, a needle and some knives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle in London is one of these monuments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is called a needle, as with Cleopatra's Needle.

clue.text: Service paymasters with English sailors present

parts.note: the MoD, the UK Ministry of Defence, pays the armed services
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Military pay offices with English navy men are on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Present as an adjective means current, belonging to now, the same as up-to-date.

clue.text: Crown of every tenth tree blighted SW city

indicators.note: the crown is the top, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: blighted means spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The top of one tree in every ten is diseased.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city of Devon lies in south-west England.
